summary: UK conventions. A two-page CV is normal and expected; a personal profile at the top is standard practice.

photo.note: Photos are not expected on UK CVs and are best omitted; UK employers avoid anything that could be read as a basis for discrimination.

personalInfo.note: Date of birth, marital status, gender and nationality are not included on a UK CV. City is useful; a full street address is not.

page.note: Two pages is the standard expectation. A one-page CV reads as early-career; three is acceptable for senior or academic candidates.

notes: Most large UK employers and recruiters use ATS software; keep headings conventional and the layout single-column for those applications.
UK spelling should be used when applying to UK employers (organisation, analyse, programme).
A UK CV usually opens with a short personal profile (two to four lines) rather than a US-style headline.
Achievement-oriented bullets are expected, but a slightly more formal register than a US resume reads better.

advisories.text: A short personal profile at the top is conventional in the UK and is a good place to state your specialism and years of experience.
"References available on request" is still common in the UK and is included by many candidates.
UK spelling is common for UK employers; a mix of US and UK spelling can read as an untailored application, so it is usually worth keeping one style throughout.
Degree classification (First, 2:1) is often expected from recent graduates and can be omitted once you have several years of experience.
